To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have experimentally demonstrated the existence of a bandgap in the transmission of acoustic waves in a periodically modulated waveguide, and that we have experimentically demonstrated the existence of defect modes within the band gap.

the transmission of sound through a periodic array of circular waveguides can be controlled by changing the periodicity and that the introduction of defects in this system results in narrow frequency bands of transmission within the forbidden band gaps, known as defect states.

(1) a band gap exists for the periodic system, (2) the presence of defects in the periodicity leads to a defect mode within the band gap, (3) the defect modes are highly localized to the region of the defect and (4) the defect modes exhibit a strong frequency dependence on the defect size and shape.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new acoustic metamaterials with novel properties.
the propagation of sound in periodic waveguide systems and how the introduction of a defect in the periodicity affects the transmission of sound.
a new type of acoustic waveguide array which is capable of producing a band gap in the frequency spectrum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transmission of sound in the periodic waveguide array is strongly affected by the periodicity of the structure, with the presence of band gap frequencies in which the transmission is forbidden and defect frequencies within the band gaps where transmission is allowed.
the results presented in this thesis have shown that it is possible to design and fabricate acoustic band gap structures and that these structures can be used to create defect modes.
the transmission spectra of the periodic arrays exhibit the presence of bandgaps, which are the result of the interference of the propagating modes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the acoustic band gap phenomenon can be observed experimentally in one-dimensional waveguide arrays.
the presence of defects in a periodic system leads to a new class of modes, called defect states.
the introduction of defects in a periodic structure leads to a localized transmission band within a band gap.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can design a waveguide system that will transmit or not transmit acoustic energy based on frequency.
it demonstrates the potential of acoustic waveguides to be used as a tool to control acoustic waves in the same way that optical waveguides are used to control light.
the presence of band-gaps and defect modes can be exploited for the design of new acoustic devices.
